findings.gate: Craft core — continuity persistence; charter §3.1 (the cataloguing narrator); packet scene_shape.turn

draft_evidence.quote: The four above the plane had a fifth. Not on the steps; on the landing at the cut's head ... and Cael had counted six and had had six, four and two, and had been wrong by one, because the sixth had been the one you do not count until he speaks.

comparison_evidence.quote: Six of them, faceless, hooded, a crossbow and staves; a sixth on the landing to say when.

findings.consequence: The arithmetic does not close. Four at the top (L9) plus two at the bottom (L9) is six; adding a fifth above who is not on the steps makes seven, which the draft itself concedes ('had been wrong by one') and then never carries: the new man is labelled 'the sixth' (L65, L79), the team is 'six people' at L71 and 'six hoods' at L81, and the log records 'Six of them ... a sixth on the landing' (L125). L79 compounds it — 'the six of them were six shapes on a landing' — while the other two are still on the steps below and only get up in the following clause, so five people are counted as six. The packet's own staging makes the coordinator one of the six ('removes the man who was coordinating the six', packet L547). This is the one error this narrator cannot afford: counting is his first competence, established in the chapter's second sentence ('a cataloguer walks a thing eleven times so that he has it on the twelfth', L3), and a reader who counts along — which the book trains them to do — is left holding seven while the log says six.
findings.repair_target: L65, L71, L79, L81, L125 — pick one arithmetic and hold it. Cheapest repair: make the signaller one of the four already counted (three came down onto the first flight, the fourth stayed on the landing to say when), which keeps the total at six, keeps 'the sixth' honest as a label, keeps L125 as written, and preserves the beat that Cael miscounted what each of them was for rather than how many there were. If the seventh is wanted, L71, L79, L81 and L125 must all be re-counted and 'the sixth' renamed.

findings.gate: Charter §4.1 (geography drawable); combat module gate 2; packet obligation 'watching Iron Wall from two feet'

draft_evidence.quote: He had stood two feet from it. That was the fact. He had stood on the third flight at the plane's foot for the length of a fight ... and had watched, from two feet, a Silver-tier Iron Wall held across a corridor by a man who could not move and would not stop

comparison_evidence.quote: and it was, Cael saw — from six feet below it, looking up — the first thing he had ever watched Iron Wall do that the ground did not argue with.

findings.consequence: The chapter fixes Cael's distance from the plane three times and gets two different numbers. The plane is set 'from the second flight's top step' with Vastin on the second flight (L25); Cael is on the third flight (L11, L55); L27 measures that as six feet below the plane; L85 measures the same gap again — 'Cael, who was six feet below him ... went up the six feet and sat down on the step beside him' — and then L103 twice calls it two feet. Two feet is not a decorative number: it is the staging condition the packet (L535) and the card (L1256) impose on the integration, so the beat the whole chapter is built to deliver rests on the one measurement the chapter contradicts. A reader drawing the fight, which charter §4.1 requires them to be able to do, hits it at the climax.
findings.repair_target: L27, L85, L103 — one distance, used three times. Either move Cael up to the plane's foot on the second flight when the boxes go down (which makes 'at the plane's foot' literal and lets L85 read 'two feet below him'), or keep him on the third flight and change L103's 'two feet' to the distance the chapter has already established — but the second option needs the packet's two-feet condition released at the planning layer first.

findings.gate: Charter §9 anti-tic list; packet prohibited_outcomes ('capped phrases 0')

draft_evidence.quote: and stood at a plane with their hoods up and a crossbow they had spent and a leader who had gone quiet, and were, for the length of a breath, six people who did not know what to do.

comparison_evidence.quote: no modern idiom; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; 'upside down' 0; capped phrases 0; no meta-voice; READER STANDARD.

findings.consequence: 'for the length of a breath' carries a hard cap of zero in this packet, stated twice (L539 and L579), because the phrase has already reached watermark density in the series — B7 Ch13 uses it too (packet L248). One verbatim use survives at L71, and the near-variant 'in the length of a breath' at L79 sits eight lines away, so the two land inside the same movement and a listener hears the repetition as a tic rather than a measure. This is an explicit packet prohibition, not a matter of taste.
findings.repair_target: L71 and L79 — replace both with different measures of the same short interval, and make them different from each other (the chapter already owns better instruments: a count, a step, a breath drawn, the time a man takes to work at a cord).

findings.gate: Packet obligations.must_include — 'The faction's knowledge stated in Cael's register'

draft_evidence.quote: "They'll go to ground and think. They know where we sleep now. They knew before, but now they know we know." ... "They came for a declaration. They got a wall and a rock. They don't know what to make of that, and they'll want to."

comparison_evidence.quote: The faction's knowledge stated in Cael's register: they know the crew's movements now; they do not know what works inside the Quiet; they saw an alley.

findings.consequence: One of the obligation's three parts is on the page, and it is in Seln's mouth rather than in Cael's cataloguing register. The two missing parts are the ones that carry forward: the card's whole point about this fight is that 'its knowledge of what works inside the Quiet still zero ... it saw a fight in an alley; it did not see quiet ground' (packet L1254). Scope searched: every occurrence of 'quiet ground' and 'the Quiet' in the draft — L11, L43, L55 — and all three describe what the team believes about the crew walking OUT declaring, which is the team's knowledge, not the limit of it. Nothing anywhere states that the encounter taught them nothing about the inside. Without it the chapter reads as a straightforward repelled ambush and the series' central asymmetry — the Compact's ignorance of the one thing that matters — is not banked where the architecture banks it, which weakens Ch21's last reach on the road.
findings.repair_target: The aftermath movement, L97-103 — add one sentence in Cael's register after Seln's assessment, entering the limit as a finding, not an aside: what the six now hold (the inn, the hour, the route) set against what they still do not (what happens to a Path inside quiet ground), and that what they saw tonight was an alley.

findings.gate: Charter §5.5; LitRPG module gate 2 (values match the approved state snapshot)

draft_evidence.quote: Iron-Wall-adjacent. Vastin. Partial. Iron. Held. A plane, not a body: the ground told not to give. ... Engagement field: defensive; rooted. Tier equivalent unknown. Deployment: none. Eleventh.

findings.consequence: The fourth slot of this book's notice format carries a tier: ch13.md L95 gives 'Bronze' for Cleon, ch19.md L67 gives 'Bronze' for Teague, and B7 Ch13's exemplar labels the field outright ('Tier equivalent: Iron', packet L232). Read that way, L109 declares 'Iron' and then, eleven words later, 'Tier equivalent unknown' — the same field answered twice, incompatibly, inside one four-line notice. Read the other way, as the source's tier, it is simply wrong: Vastin's plane is 'a Silver-tier plane' in this chapter's own prose (L85) and 'a Silver-tier rooted declaration' in the packet. The only reading that saves it is 'Iron' as a Path family, which neither sibling notice supports. A reader keeping the sheet the series invites them to keep (§5.5) cannot record this fragment's tier, and the packet's own list of required notice fields (L557) does not include a fourth-slot tier at all.
findings.repair_target: L109 — drop the fourth slot, or replace 'Iron' with the family marker made explicit ('Iron family') so it cannot be read as the tier field that the notice then declares unknown. The packet requires only: Iron-Wall-adjacent; from Vastin; partial; holding not hardening; tier equivalent unknown; engagement field held/defensive.

findings.gate: Packet obligations.must_include — win-sentence on the page; exchange 2 ('Cael and Brom are the reason they want the line')

draft_evidence.quote: and every one of the four wanted through that plane worse than they wanted anything, because he was on the other side of it, and the wanting was the cost of the plane, and he was the cost.

comparison_evidence.quote: the team's second element comes at the wall's protected side from below expecting declarations and meets people — Brom's rock and back, Lira's knife in no room, Cael silent; Cael and Brom are the reason they want the line (Ch4's lesson paid)

findings.consequence: The win-sentence's second clause is a pair — 'Cael and Brom removed their ability to ignore it' — and only Cael is delivered. Brom's whole function in exchange 2 is defensive: he meets a stave, puts a man into the wall, stands on the stave and does not hit him again (L47). Nowhere is he a reason the two from below come up, and the two from below in fact come up before Cael's stillness is described, so the draft supplies no motive for that half of the attack at all — they simply arrive. Ch4's lesson, which the chapter is built to pay, was learned by two men on that road (Cael on the scree and Brom silent with a rock at the plane's south end, ch04.md L105-119); paying it with one of them halves the payoff and leaves exchange 2's causality thinner than exchanges 1 and 3, which are exact.
findings.repair_target: L43-47 — one clause giving the two from below their reason: the big one who righted a broker's cart in a yard where anyone could watch, and the boy from the report, both on the wall's protected side. It also fixes the missing motive for their approach.

findings.gate: Charter §9 (any repeated beat phrase, including a newly invented one, is capped)

draft_evidence.quote: a Silver-tier plane held across a cut for the length of a fight is not a plane held across a road for the length of a charge

comparison_evidence.quote: because he had sat beside it for the length of the man's breath coming back. ... He had stood on the third flight at the plane's foot for the length of a fight

findings.consequence: Counted over the whole draft, 'for/in the length of a [X]' runs five times — L71, L79, L85 (twice in one clause), L101, L103 — in a 4,395-word chapter. Charter §9's rule is explicit that fixing a tic with a fresh repeated phrase is the same defect in a different coat, and the cap is three per book, not per chapter. Four of the five sit in the chapter's last third, so they cluster where the prose is meant to slow and land; on audio the construction starts to announce itself as the narrator's measuring habit rather than a measure.
findings.repair_target: L79, L85, L101 — vary three of the five. L85's doubled use inside one comparison is the loudest and should go first; the chapter already has a better instrument for duration in Cael's literal count.

draft_evidence.quote: the thing had gone into him the way the nine had gone in — not taken; *learned*, at two feet, by a body that learned the shape of a thing by standing beside it long enough

comparison_evidence.quote: the current went along the ten and came to the place where the ten bent, and he felt them bend — Wind going round it, Iron going round it, all ten going round a thing

findings.consequence: The book counts Cael's fragments as ten and says so repeatedly — 'the ten frameworks knocking together in him' (ch04.md L149), 'all ten going round' (ch07.md L37), 'ten things in him' in this chapter's own L11. 'The nine' arrives at the chapter's most important moment with no antecedent and no gloss. It is probably deliberate — the nine taken in the field, as against the tenth, Tide, which came clinically on a table — but that distinction is nowhere on the page, and the appositive that follows ('not taken; learned') actually describes Tide's acquisition better than it describes the nine that came out of fights. A listener, who cannot glance back, is left doing arithmetic during the integration.
findings.repair_target: L107 — either restore 'the ten', or keep 'the nine' and name what excludes the tenth in the same clause (the one that came on a table under a healer's hands).

findings.gate: Craft core reader-trust invariant 1 (inference must read as inference)

draft_evidence.quote: No healer inside the gate would put hands on an unranked woman's hand. Oryn had said so, at a fire, and had been right, and the cost of it was a strip of shirt and Brom's teeth

comparison_evidence.quote: If you use it and it goes, there's no healer inside that gate who'll put hands on a Copper's shoulder, because inside that gate there's a column, and you're at the bottom of it.

findings.consequence: Oryn priced a Copper's shoulder, not an unranked woman's hand. The extension is sound — Karis is unranked by choice and stands below the column's bottom rung — but the draft reports it as something Oryn said rather than something Cael has worked out from what she said, which is the one move this narrator is not supposed to make. It also quietly wastes the sharper version: Oryn's rule applied to someone she was not talking about is a harder fact than Oryn's rule quoted.
findings.repair_target: L91 — one clause turning the report into the inference it is ('Oryn had priced a Copper's shoulder at a fire; a hand with no column at all was the same arithmetic, further down').

concerns: Fragment-notice format is a planning question, not an author defect, and needs a human ruling before Book 8 closes. B7 Ch13 and the Universe Bible render notices as a fenced block with a 'FRAGMENT ACQUIRED' header, a bracketed name and labelled fields; this packet instructs italic prose with no stat block (L535), and ch12/ch13/ch19 all follow the prose form consistently. The book is internally coherent and the series is not. Charter §5.2 calls format canon; charter §8.3 prefers the prose. Somebody above this seat should decide which, and whether B7's block gets retro-fitted or B8's prose gets an exception logged.

The packet's opposition includes 'one Anchor course laid across the alley's bottom step — allowed once' and the draft uses none, substituting a spoken signal and Seln's cord. The author declares the deviation. Nothing in must_include requires the course and the substitution is cleaner (it gives Seln a physical object to remove rather than a magical one), but it does mean this chapter shows the faceless faction with no practitioner capability at all — six people with staves, knives and a crossbow — which makes them read as hired muscle rather than the team from B7 Ch19 that laid an Anchor lattice across a perimeter. Worth a planning glance before Ch21 asks the reader to fear them again.

The generalising aphorism scaffold 'because a [noun] [verb]s' runs seven times (L11, L51, L63, L69, L79, L97, L121), plus close cousins at L17 ('because a party that put its boxes down was a party that...'), L27 ('because they were men and men do not') and L69 ('because nobody in a city looks up'). This is house voice and mostly earns itself, but at ten instances in 4,395 words it starts to read as a generator rather than a habit of mind. Not a contract violation; flagged so a line pass can thin two or three of the weaker ones.

Paragraph length is very long even for this voice — L79 runs 236 words, L25 228, L47 209, L5 203, L27 203 — and four of those five are inside the fight. Charter §Sentence music asks for cadence contrast and the combat module names 'sudden stopping' as an available register. The chapter does use short paragraphs well at its hinges (L45 'Nobody declared.', L67 'Seln removed it.', L99 'And Vastin.'), so the tools are there; the middle of each exchange could take one more of them.

'he had walked the alley eleven times' (L3) sits against 'had been right for eight days' (L5). Eight days of one descent each evening does not obviously produce eleven walks; two directions a day produces sixteen. It is reconcilable (the archive week did not start on the first day in the city) and no state document fixes the number, so this is not a finding — but the sentence draws attention to the count deliberately, which invites the reader to check it.

Vastin's Ch10 reflex — the name, the title, the rank — is paid off silently and beautifully here: he holds a wall for a party and never says a word about who he is, and Seln's 'Be nobody' is never quoted at him. Preserve this. A repair pass tempted to make the payoff explicit would kill it.
strengths: The corridor genuinely rewards the wall, and the draft proves it rather than asserting it: 'On a road the ground had said *go round*. Here the ground said *there is no round*.' (L27) is the whole Ch4-to-Ch12 argument in eleven words, and it is followed by the mechanism — sheer walls, no scree, and 'every other way to the party was round by the ring road and up through the yard gate, which was a hundred strides and a minute' (L31). The reader can check the arithmetic of the win, which is the series' contract.

Seln's beat is the best-constructed thing in the chapter. It is set up before it is used ('Seln was not anywhere. Good.', L13), reconstructed honestly rather than witnessed ('Cael did not see it. He saw the result ... and drew the rest afterward', L63), and its removal is a cord round an arm rather than a body — 'Nobody died. Nobody was cut. The signal stopped.' (L69). The cache reveal lands on the same move: 'The cache was on the roof. It had been on the roof the whole time, on a man's back, unopened, and the four had come for it, and it had been above them, and they had never once looked up.' (L73). Three obligations paid by one image.

The crew's conduct under the reader standard is not merely compliant, it is characterising. Brom stands on a stave instead of hitting a man twice (L47); Lira puts a knife into a shaft and the flat across a knee, and Cael watches her choose it ('the knife did not go into him — Cael saw that, and saw her choose it', L51); and the two beaten men are allowed to walk out through the party's own side 'because the party let them, because Brom stood on the stave and Lira stood on the step and neither of them touched a man who was walking away' (L79). Mercy is shown as competence, which is exactly the register the standard asks for.

The costs are priced in the crew's own vocabulary rather than narrated. Karis's whole report on her cut is 'The sheets are dry' (L91); Brom's is 'Cart was heavier' (L93); Lira's is a hand opening and closing and letting herself be caught looking (L95). Brom binding a hand badly 'with his good hand and his teeth ... like a man who has watched a healer do it a hundred times and has never once been the hands' is the no-healer decision from Ch6 paid in full, concretely, without anyone mentioning the decision.

Vastin's aftermath speech earns the chapter's title without touching it. 'There was nothing behind it. I have never once in my life held a line with nothing behind it' and 'I know what you are, on the paper. I have read the paper more times than any man alive. I put the wall in front of it anyway. I'd like that entered somewhere, since I'm not the one who keeps the ledger any more.' (L115, L119) is a man with no authority asking to be entered in someone else's record — the exact inversion the book is built on, said obliquely, with the thematic statement left off the page.

The closing move refuses the easy landing: Cael writes it down and does not tell Vastin what else he entered, 'because a fragment is a thing you own and a thing a man gave you is a thing you owe, and he did not yet have a word for the distance between those two, and was not going to make one up on a step' (L121). It sets the debt live for Book 9 and hands the fixed log a reason to exist rather than a summary to repeat.

Mechanical hygiene is clean: word count 4,395 in a 3,910-5,290 band; the fixed closing log matches the card character for character; zero one-word paragraphs; 'the way X [verb]' at 2 of 4; 'upside down', 'at the pitch', 'four hundred' and all four forbidden names at zero; no authoring metadata; no mule; no station, square, clerk or registry.
